source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

chapters.source_omission_reason: Absent from pinned SBLGNT; the parent Fluent already preserves this numbering gap.
chapters.tsw_omission_reason: TSW also lacks these public labels; comparator bytes unchanged.

verses.rationale: Keeps the renewed teaching and the crowd as the reason for the boat; locates both teacher and listeners.
verses.before: Jesus began teaching beside the sea again. Such a large crowd gathered around him that he got into a boat and sat in it on the sea, while the whole crowd stayed on the shore.
verses.after: Jesus began teaching beside the sea again. Such a large crowd gathered around him that he got into a boat and sat in it out on the water, while the whole crowd stayed on the shore.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again he began to teach beside the sea. Such a very large crowd gathered around him that he got into a boat on the sea and sat there, while the whole crowd was beside the sea on the land.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated teaching frame and identifies the following speech as a parable.
verses.before: He taught them many things in parables. In his teaching he said,
verses.after: He taught them many things in parables. As he taught, he said,
verses.tsw_comparator: And he taught them many things in parables, and in his teaching he said to them:

verses.rationale: Carries both attention commands and renders the substantival sower naturally without losing sowing.
verses.before: “Listen! A sower went out to sow.
verses.after: “Listen! Look, a farmer went out to sow.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Listen! A sower went out to sow.

verses.rationale: Supplies seed as the object implicit in sowing; keeps the first location and the birds’ action.
verses.before: As he sowed, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.
verses.after: As he scattered the seed, some fell beside the path, and the birds came and ate it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as he sowed, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.

verses.rationale: Makes the lack of soil the explicit cause of rapid sprouting, not a later explanation.
verses.before: Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.
verses.after: Other seed fell on rocky ground, where there was little soil. It sprang up at once because the soil was shallow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil, and it sprang up quickly, since it had no depth of soil.

verses.rationale: Keeps scorching and lack of root distinct and makes the causal link audible.
verses.before: When the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered.
verses.after: When the sun rose, it was scorched. It had no root, so it withered.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the sun rose, it was scorched; and since it had no root, it withered away.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three-step failure: competing growth, choking, and no fruit.
verses.before: Other seed fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked it, and it produced no grain.
verses.after: Other seed fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked it, and it produced no crop.
verses.tsw_comparator: Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no grain.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ascending three yields without correcting their exuberance.
verses.before: Other seed fell into good soil and produced grain, growing and increasing and yielding thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold.”
verses.after: Still other seed fell on good soil. It grew and flourished, producing a crop—thirty, sixty, and a hundred times what was sown.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Other seed fell into good soil and produced grain, growing up and increasing and yielding thirty and sixty and a hundredfold.”

verses.rationale: Retains the bodily image and the invitation’s general scope.
verses.before: Then he said, “Let anyone who has ears to hear listen.”
verses.after: Then he said, “Anyone with ears to hear should listen!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “Let anyone with ears to hear listen.”

verses.rationale: Does not reduce the questioners to the Twelve; follows plural parables in the pinned text.
verses.before: When Jesus was alone, those around him with the twelve asked him about the parables.
verses.after: When he was alone, those around him, along with the Twelve, asked him about the parables.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he was alone, those around him together with the twelve asked him about the parables.

verses.rationale: Retains the passive gift, mystery, and insider–outsider contrast without adding a theory of exclusion.
verses.before: He said to them, “To you has been given the mystery of the kingdom of God, but for those outside everything comes in parables,
verses.after: He told them, “The mystery of God’s kingdom has been given to you. But for those outside, everything comes in parables,
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “To you has been given the mystery of the reign of God, but for those outside, everything comes in parables,

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult purpose and prevention language rather than replacing it with because; repeated verbs remain audible.
verses.before: so that ‘they may indeed look but not perceive, and may indeed hear but not understand, lest they turn and be forgiven.’”
verses.after: so that ‘they may look and look but not see, and listen and listen but not understand, lest they turn back and be forgiven.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: so that ‘they may indeed look, but not perceive, and may indeed hear, but not understand, lest they turn again and be forgiven.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps the two questions and their inferential connection.
verses.before: Then he said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?
verses.after: Then he said to them, “Don’t you understand this parable? How, then, will you understand all the parables?
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand all the parables?

verses.rationale: Retains word as the recurring interpretive term rather than changing it verse by verse.
verses.before: “The sower sows the word.
verses.after: The farmer sows the word.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The sower sows the word.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the shift from seeds to hearers while retaining Satan and immediate removal.
verses.before: These are the ones along the path where the word is sown: when they hear, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word sown in them.
verses.after: Some are like the seed beside the path, where the word is sown. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word sown in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the ones along the path, where the word is sown: when they hear, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word that is sown in them.

verses.rationale: Keeps joyful immediate reception distinct from the later failure.
verses.before: These are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy.
verses.after: Others are like the seed sown on rocky ground. When they hear the word, they receive it with joy at once.
verses.tsw_comparator: And these are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy.

verses.rationale: Preserves the root image and persecution’s connection to the word; does not make trouble generic.
verses.before: But they have no root in themselves and last only for a while. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately fall away.
verses.after: But they have no root in themselves and last only a little while. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they fall away at once.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they have no root in themselves, and endure only for a while; then, when trouble or persecution arises on account of the word, immediately they fall away.

verses.rationale: Keeps the third category and carries its sentence into the next verse.
verses.before: Others are the ones sown among thorns. They hear the word,
verses.after: Still others are like the seed sown among thorns. They hear the word,
verses.tsw_comparator: And others are the ones sown among thorns: these are those who hear the word,

verses.rationale: Retains all three intrusions and wealth’s deceptive quality, not simply possession of wealth.
verses.before: but the cares of the age, the lure of wealth, and desires for other things enter in and choke the word, making it unfruitful.
verses.after: but the worries of this age, the deceitfulness of wealth, and desires for other things come in and choke the word, and it bears no fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: but the cares of the age, and the lure of wealth, and the desires for other things come in and choke the word, and it proves unfruitful.

verses.rationale: Repeats the same yields as verse 8 and preserves hearing, accepting, and bearing fruit as distinct acts.
verses.before: But the ones sown on good soil hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit—thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold.”
verses.after: But those like the seed sown on good soil hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit—thirty, sixty, and a hundred times what was sown.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But these are the ones sown on good soil: they hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirty and sixty and a hundredfold.”

verses.rationale: Makes the lamp’s coming idiomatic while preserving the household objects and paired questions.
verses.before: He said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under a basket or under a bed? Is it not put on a lampstand?
verses.after: He also said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under a measuring basket or under a bed? Isn’t it brought in to be put on a lampstand?
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under a basket, or under a bed, and not to be put on a lampstand?

verses.rationale: Retains the purposive paradox rather than reducing it to a prediction of eventual discovery.
verses.before: Nothing is hidden except to be revealed, and nothing is concealed except to come into the open.
verses.after: For nothing is hidden except to be revealed, and nothing is kept secret except to come into the open.
verses.tsw_comparator: For nothing is hidden except to be made manifest, nor is anything secret except to come to light.

verses.rationale: Repeats the hearing refrain consistently with verse 9.
verses.before: If anyone has ears to hear, listen.”
verses.after: Anyone with ears to hear should listen!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Let anyone with ears to hear listen.”

verses.rationale: Keeps what rather than how; preserves the measure image and the added gift.
verses.before: He also said, “Pay attention to what you hear. The measure you use will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.
verses.after: He went on, “Pay attention to what you hear. The measure you use will be used for you, and more will be given to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Pay attention to what you hear; the measure you give will be the measure you receive, and still more will be given to you.

verses.rationale: Leaves the unspecified possession open and retains the saying’s unsettling contrast.
verses.before: For whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken away.”
verses.after: For whoever has will be given more; whoever does not have will lose even what they have.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For to those who have, more will be given; and from those who have nothing, even what they have will be taken away.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the human sowing comparison without identifying the sower allegorically.
verses.before: Jesus said, “The kingdom of God is like this: someone scatters seed on the ground.
verses.after: He also said, “God’s kingdom is like someone scattering seed on the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “The reign of God is as if someone would scatter seed on the ground,

verses.rationale: Keeps ordinary repeated life alongside growth that the sower cannot explain.
verses.before: Night and day, whether that person sleeps or gets up, the seed sprouts and grows, though the person does not know how.
verses.after: Night and day, the person sleeps and gets up, while the seed sprouts and grows—though the person does not know how.
verses.tsw_comparator: and would sleep and rise night and day, and the seed would sprout and grow—he does not know how.

verses.rationale: Retains automatic growth and the three agricultural stages.
verses.before: The earth produces by itself—first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain in the head.
verses.after: The ground produces a crop on its own: first the shoot, then the head, then the full grain in the head.
verses.tsw_comparator: The earth produces of itself, first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain in the head.

verses.rationale: Carries immediate harvesting, the sickle image, and the stated reason.
verses.before: But as soon as the grain is ready, the person sends in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
verses.after: As soon as the crop is ready, the farmer puts in the sickle, because harvest time has come.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the grain is ripe, at once he goes in with the sickle, because the harvest has come.”

verses.rationale: Retains the paired deliberative questions and inclusive we.
verses.before: He said, “How can we compare the kingdom of God? What parable can we use for it?
verses.after: He also said, “What can we compare God’s kingdom to? What parable can we use for it?
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “With what can we compare the reign of God, or what parable will we use for it?

verses.rationale: Preserves the comparison’s unqualified superlative instead of silently modernizing its botanical scope.
verses.before: It is like a mustard seed, which when sown on the ground is among the smallest of the seeds on earth.
verses.after: It is like a mustard seed. When sown in the ground, it is the smallest of all the seeds on earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown upon the ground, is the smallest of all the seeds on earth;

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrast with garden plants, not trees, and the nesting birds beneath its shade.
verses.before: Yet after it is sown, it grows up and becomes greater than the other garden plants and puts out large branches, so that the birds of the air can nest in its shade.”
verses.after: Yet once sown, it grows and becomes larger than all the garden plants. It puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can nest in its shade.”
verses.tsw_comparator: yet when it is sown it grows up and becomes the greatest of all shrubs, and puts forth large branches, so that the birds of the air can make nests in its shade.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the listeners’ capacity and word as the subject of the teaching.
verses.before: With many parables like these he spoke the word to them as they were able to hear it.
verses.after: With many parables like these, he spoke the word to them, as much as they were able to hear.
verses.tsw_comparator: With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the public–private contrast without universalizing it beyond this narrative setting.
verses.before: He did not speak to them without a parable, but in private he explained everything to his own disciples.
verses.after: He did not speak to them without a parable, but privately he explained everything to his own disciples.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did not speak to them except in parables, but he explained everything in private to his disciples.

verses.rationale: Retains the same-day link and the invitation to cross.
verses.before: That day, when evening came, he said to them, “Let us cross over to the other side.”
verses.after: That same day, when evening came, he said to them, “Let’s cross to the other side.”
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, “Let us go across to the other side.”

verses.rationale: Retains the unusual just-as-he-was detail and the otherwise unexplained accompanying boats.
verses.before: Leaving the crowd, they took him with them in the boat just as he was. Other boats were with him.
verses.after: Leaving the crowd behind, they took him along in the boat, just as he was. Other boats were with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And leaving the crowd behind, they took him with them in the boat, just as he was. Other boats were with him.

verses.rationale: Keeps wind, waves, and the boat’s immediate danger rather than a generic storm summary.
verses.before: A great windstorm arose, and the waves were breaking into the boat so that it was already filling.
verses.after: A fierce windstorm arose, and waves broke into the boat until it was already filling with water.
verses.tsw_comparator: A great windstorm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so that the boat was already being swamped.

verses.rationale: Names Jesus for clarity while retaining the stern, cushion, and accusatory question.
verses.before: Jesus was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. They woke him and said, “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”
verses.after: Jesus was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. They woke him and said, “Teacher, don’t you care that we’re perishing?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him up and said to him, “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”

verses.rationale: Retains rebuke and the two commands; great calm answers the great storm.
verses.before: He got up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Quiet! Be still!” The wind stopped, and there was a great calm.
verses.after: He woke up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Be quiet! Be still!” The wind died down, and there was a great calm.
verses.tsw_comparator: He woke up and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” Then the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned not-yet wording and does not substitute little faith from another account.
verses.before: He said to them, “Why are you afraid? Do you still have no faith?”
verses.after: He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “Why are you afraid? Have you still no trust?”

verses.rationale: Preserves intensified fear after the calm and the unresolved identity question.
verses.before: They were filled with great fear and said to one another, “Who then is this? Even the wind and the sea obey him!”
verses.after: They were overcome with fear and said to one another, “Who is this, then? Even the wind and the sea obey him!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they were filled with great fear and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

verses.rationale: Follows Gerasenes in the pinned text, without geographic harmonization.
verses.before: They came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.
verses.after: They reached the other side of the sea, in the region of the Gerasenes.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.

verses.rationale: Names the boat’s departing subject and retains immediate encounter and unclean spirit.
verses.before: As soon as Jesus stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit came from the tombs to meet him.
verses.after: As soon as Jesus stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit came from the tombs to meet him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as he came out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met him from the tombs.

verses.rationale: Keeps the habitation and the escalating failure of restraint.
verses.before: The man lived among the tombs, and no one could bind him anymore, not even with a chain.
verses.after: The man lived among the tombs. No one could restrain him anymore, not even with a chain.
verses.tsw_comparator: He lived among the tombs, and no one was able to bind him anymore, not even with a chain,

verses.rationale: Distinguishes prior repeated binding, destroyed restraints, and inability to subdue.
verses.before: He had often been bound with shackles and chains, but he tore the chains apart and shattered the shackles. No one was strong enough to subdue him.
verses.after: He had often been bound with shackles and chains, but he had torn the chains apart and smashed the shackles. No one was strong enough to subdue him.
verses.tsw_comparator: for he had often been bound with shackles and chains, but the chains had been torn apart by him and the shackles shattered, and no one had the strength to subdue him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ongoing distress and concrete self-injury without euphemism or diagnosis.
verses.before: Night and day he was always among the tombs and on the mountains, crying out and cutting himself with stones.
verses.after: Night and day, among the tombs and in the hills, he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones.
verses.tsw_comparator: And constantly, night and day, among the tombs and on the mountains, he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.

verses.rationale: Renders the bodily act without deciding that it expresses worshipful allegiance.
verses.before: When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before him.
verses.after: When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And seeing Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down before him,

verses.rationale: Makes the confrontational idiom natural but preserves the adjuration by God and full title.
verses.before: Crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I implore you by God, do not torment me!”
verses.after: He shouted at the top of his voice, “What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I put you under oath by God: do not torment me!”
verses.tsw_comparator: and crying out with a loud voice he said, “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, do not torment me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the explanatory backward movement and distinguishes man from spirit.
verses.before: For Jesus had been saying to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit.”
verses.after: For Jesus had been saying to him, “Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!”
verses.tsw_comparator: For he was saying to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit.”

verses.rationale: Retains the singular-to-plural shift and leaves the unsettling reply intact.
verses.before: Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He answered, “My name is Legion, because we are many.”
verses.after: Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He answered, “My name is Legion, because we are many.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he asked him, “What is your name?” And he said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”

verses.rationale: Preserves singular pleading about plural spirits instead of smoothing away the shift.
verses.before: And he begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of the region.
verses.after: He begged Jesus insistently not to send them out of the region.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he begged him earnestly not to send them out of the region.

verses.rationale: Keeps the herd’s size and hillside location.
verses.before: A large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside.
verses.after: A large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now there was there on the hillside a great herd of pigs feeding,

verses.rationale: Makes the plural speakers clear from context while retaining both requested actions.
verses.before: The spirits begged him, “Send us into the pigs so that we may enter them.”
verses.after: The spirits begged him, “Send us into the pigs. Let us enter them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and they begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs; let us enter them.”

verses.rationale: Retains permission, approximate number, steep descent, and death of the animals.
verses.before: Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, and the herd—about two thousand—rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned.
verses.after: He allowed them. The unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, and the herd—about two thousand—rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he permitted them. And coming out, the unclean spirits entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, about two thousand, and were drowned in the sea.

verses.rationale: Keeps both places of reporting and the resulting arrival of observers.
verses.before: Those tending the pigs fled and reported it in the city and countryside, and people came to see what had happened.
verses.after: The herders ran away and reported what had happened in the town and countryside. People came to see.
verses.tsw_comparator: And those who tended them fled and reported it in the city and in the countryside. And they came to see what it was that had happened.

verses.rationale: Preserves the narrator’s description without a modern medical label and keeps the observers’ surprising fear.
verses.before: They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been demonized sitting there, clothed and in his right mind—the man who had had the legion—and they were afraid.
verses.after: They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been possessed by demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind—the man who had had the legion. And they were afraid.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they came to Jesus and saw the one who had been demonized sitting, clothed and in his right mind—the one who had had the legion—and they were afraid.

verses.rationale: Keeps both the human restoration and the animal loss in the witnesses’ account.
verses.before: Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the demonized man and to the pigs.
verses.after: Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the man possessed by demons and to the pigs.
verses.tsw_comparator: And those who had seen it described to them what had happened to the one who had been demonized and about the pigs.

verses.rationale: Makes the new pleading speakers clear and preserves their request to leave.
verses.before: Then they began begging Jesus to leave their region.
verses.after: Then the people began begging Jesus to leave their territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they began to beg him to depart from their region.

verses.rationale: Keeps the man’s contrasting request and the simple be-with-him language.
verses.before: As Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who had been demonized begged to go with him.
verses.after: As Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by demons begged to be with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as he was getting into the boat, the one who had been demonized begged him that he might be with him.

verses.rationale: Retains refusal, homeward commission, Lord, and mercy without substituting a narrower family referent.
verses.before: Jesus did not allow him but said, “Go home to your own people and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and how he had mercy on you.”
verses.after: Jesus did not let him. Instead, he said, “Go home to your own people and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and how he has shown you mercy.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he did not permit him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your own, and report to them what the Lord has done for you and how he had mercy on you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the movement from Lord in the command to Jesus in the report and leaves Decapolis as a named region.
verses.before: The man went away and began proclaiming throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.
verses.after: The man went away and began proclaiming throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. Everyone was amazed.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis what Jesus had done for him, and all were amazed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the return crossing and shore setting for the interwoven stories.
verses.before: When Jesus had crossed again by boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around him beside the sea.
verses.after: Jesus crossed back to the other side in the boat. A large crowd gathered around him, and he stayed beside the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when Jesus had crossed again in the boat to the other side, a great crowd gathered around him, and he was beside the sea.

verses.rationale: Retains one-of-the-leaders, the name, and the bodily plea while allowing the sentence to continue.
verses.before: One of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came. When he saw Jesus, he fell at his feet
verses.after: One of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came. When he saw Jesus, he fell at his feet
verses.tsw_comparator: And one of the synagogue rulers came, Jairus by name, and seeing him, fell at his feet,

verses.rationale: Keeps the affectionate diminutive, urgency, requested touch, and both healing and life.
verses.before: and pleaded with him earnestly, “My little daughter is near death. Come and lay your hands on her so that she may be saved and live.”
verses.after: and begged him urgently, “My little daughter is near death. Please come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be healed and live.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and begged him earnestly, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be saved and live.”

verses.rationale: Makes Jesus the traveler and retains the crowd’s pressure that frames the touch.
verses.before: Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed in around him.
verses.after: Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed, pressing in on him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he went with him. And a great crowd followed him and pressed upon him.

verses.rationale: Preserves duration and bodily suffering without introducing a diagnosis.
verses.before: A woman had been suffering from a flow of blood for twelve years.
verses.after: A woman was there who had been bleeding for twelve years.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there was a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years,

verses.rationale: Retains harm associated with treatment, exhausted resources, and worsening rather than sanitizing the account.
verses.before: She had suffered greatly under many physicians and had spent everything she had, yet instead of getting better she had grown worse.
verses.after: She had suffered a great deal under many doctors and had spent everything she had. Yet she was no better; instead, she had grown worse.
verses.tsw_comparator: and had suffered much under many physicians and had spent all that she had and was no better but rather grew worse,

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing, approach from behind, and the concrete garment touched.
verses.before: When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his cloak,
verses.after: She had heard about Jesus, and she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his cloak.
verses.tsw_comparator: having heard about Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd and touched his garment.

verses.rationale: Retains the explanatory inner speech and even the clothes rather than a required bodily touch.
verses.before: because she kept saying, “If I touch even his clothes, I will be saved.”
verses.after: For she had been saying, “If I can touch even his clothes, I will be healed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For she was saying, “If I touch even his garments, I will be saved.”

verses.rationale: Makes the dried-up flow idiomatic while preserving immediate bodily awareness.
verses.before: Immediately the flow of blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she had been healed from her affliction.
verses.after: At once her bleeding stopped, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately the flow of her blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she was healed of her affliction.

verses.rationale: Keeps the perception of outgoing power and the precise object in his question.
verses.before: Immediately Jesus knew in himself that power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”
verses.after: At once Jesus knew within himself that power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that power had gone out from him, turned in the crowd and said, “Who touched my garments?”

verses.rationale: Retains the disciples’ incredulity and their shortened quotation rather than harmonizing it.
verses.before: His disciples said to him, “You see the crowd pressing around you, and you ask, ‘Who touched me?’”
verses.after: His disciples said to him, “You can see the crowd pressing in on you, and you ask, ‘Who touched me?’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And his disciples said to him, “You see the crowd pressing upon you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”

verses.rationale: Preserves the continuing search without implying he publicly identified her already.
verses.before: But he kept looking around to see who had done it.
verses.after: But he kept looking around to see who had done it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he was looking around to see the one who had done this.

verses.rationale: Keeps knowledge, fear, bodily approach, and complete disclosure as the woman’s own actions.
verses.before: The woman, afraid and trembling because she knew what had happened to her, came and fell before him and told him the whole truth.
verses.after: The woman knew what had happened to her. Afraid and trembling, she came, fell before him, and told him the whole truth.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.

verses.rationale: Retains the kinship address and the healing sense of saved here; notes the broader verb separately.
verses.before: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace and be healed from your affliction.”
verses.after: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be free of your affliction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace, and be healed of your affliction.”

verses.rationale: Makes the message’s origin intelligible and retains its finality and discouraging question.
verses.before: While Jesus was still speaking, people came from the synagogue leader’s house and said, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any longer?”
verses.after: While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue leader’s house and said, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any longer?”
verses.tsw_comparator: While he was still speaking, they came from the house of the synagogue ruler, saying, “Your daughter has died; why trouble the teacher any longer?”

verses.rationale: Uses overheard for parakousas while retaining the consequential alternative in a note.
verses.before: But Jesus, overhearing what they said, told the synagogue leader, “Do not be afraid; only trust.”
verses.after: Jesus overheard what they were saying and told the synagogue leader, “Do not be afraid. Only believe.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jesus, overhearing what was spoken, said to the synagogue ruler, “Do not fear; only believe.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the restricted witnesses and specifies which men are brothers.
verses.before: He allowed no one to follow him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
verses.after: He let no one follow him except Peter, James, and John, James’s brother.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he permitted no one to follow him except Peter and James and John the brother of James.

verses.rationale: Names the observing subject and keeps both visible commotion and audible mourning.
verses.before: When they came to the synagogue leader’s house, Jesus saw a commotion, with people weeping and wailing loudly.
verses.after: They came to the synagogue leader’s house, and Jesus saw the commotion: people weeping and wailing loudly.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they came to the house of the synagogue ruler, and he saw a commotion, weeping and loud wailing.

verses.rationale: Preserves Jesus’ startling contrast without explaining it away in the main text.
verses.before: He went in and said to them, “Why are you making such a commotion and weeping? The child has not died but is sleeping.”
verses.after: He went inside and said to them, “Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead but sleeping.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And entering, he said to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child has not died but is sleeping.”

verses.rationale: Keeps ridicule, removal, the two parents, and the retained companions distinct.
verses.before: They laughed at him. After putting everyone outside, he took the child’s father and mother and the disciples who were with him and went in where the child was.
verses.after: They laughed at him. But he put them all outside, took the child’s father and mother and those with him, and went in where the child was.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they laughed at him. But putting them all outside, he took the father of the child and the mother and those with him and went in where the child was.

verses.rationale: Retains the Aramaic expression as transmitted by the Greek and Mark’s own translation.
verses.before: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha koum,” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up.”
verses.after: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha koum,” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And taking the child by the hand he said to her, “Talitha koum,” which is translated, “Little girl, I say to you, arise.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the girl’s age, resumed movement, and both immediacy markers.
verses.before: Immediately the girl got up and began walking around. She was twelve years old. They were overcome with great amazement.
verses.after: At once the girl got up and began walking—she was twelve years old. They were immediately overwhelmed with amazement.
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately the girl rose and began to walk, for she was twelve years old, and they were immediately overcome with great amazement.

verses.rationale: Retains both the secrecy command and the practical feeding instruction without explaining their tension.
verses.before: Jesus gave them strict orders that no one should know about this, and he told them to give her something to eat.
verses.after: He gave them strict instructions that no one should know about this, and told them to give her something to eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and he told them to give her something to eat.

verses.rationale: Names the subject and retains the disciples’ following without adding Nazareth to the source.
verses.before: Jesus left there and came to his hometown, and his disciples followed him.
verses.after: Jesus left there and came to his hometown, with his disciples following him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He went away from there and came to his hometown, and his disciples followed him.

verses.rationale: Breaks the questions into audible units while retaining given wisdom and deeds through his hands.
verses.before: When the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue. Many who heard him were astonished and said, “Where did this man get these things? What is this wisdom that has been given to him? What are these works of power being done through his hands?
verses.after: On the Sabbath he began teaching in the synagogue. Many who heard him were astonished. “Where did he get all this?” they asked. “What is this wisdom he has been given? How are miracles like these being done through his hands?
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue. Many who heard him were astounded and said, “Where did this man get these things? What is this wisdom that has been given to him? And what deeds of power are being done through his hands!

verses.rationale: Retains the pinned family names, maternal identification, brothers and sisters, and rejection.
verses.before: Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
verses.after: Isn’t this the carpenter, Mary’s son, and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three increasingly intimate locations of dishonor.
verses.before: Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own house.”
verses.after: Jesus told them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jesus said to them, “Prophets are not without honor, except in their hometown and among their kin and in their own house.”

verses.rationale: Preserves could not rather than silently changing it to would not; keeps the exception.
verses.before: He could do no work of power there except to lay his hands on a few sick people and heal them.
verses.after: He could do no miracle there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he could do no deed of power there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the cause of amazement and the transition to itinerant teaching.
verses.before: And he was amazed at their unbelief. Then he went around the surrounding villages teaching.
verses.after: He was amazed at their unbelief. Then he went around the surrounding villages, teaching.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he was amazed at their unbelief.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired sending and its specific authority.
verses.before: Jesus called the twelve and began sending them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.
verses.after: He called the Twelve to him and began sending them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.
verses.tsw_comparator: He called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.

verses.rationale: Retains Mark’s allowance of a staff and all three prohibitions without harmonizing another Gospel.
verses.before: He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts—
verses.after: He told them to take nothing for the journey except a staff—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts.
verses.tsw_comparator: He charged them to take nothing for the journey except a staff; no bread, no bag, no money in their belts;

verses.rationale: Preserves permission for sandals and the source’s shift into direct address about tunics.
verses.before: but to wear sandals and not put on two tunics.
verses.after: They were to wear sandals. “But do not wear two tunics,” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: but to wear sandals and not to put on two tunics.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes lodging in the house from departure from the locality.
verses.before: He said to them, “Whenever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.
verses.after: He told them, “Whenever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.

verses.rationale: Keeps rejection, departure, and testimony without adding a Sodom saying absent from this source.
verses.before: If any place will not welcome you or listen to you, leave and shake the dust off your feet as a testimony against them.”
verses.after: If any place will not welcome you and its people will not listen to you, leave it and shake the dust off your feet as a testimony to them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And if any place will not welcome you and they refuse to hear you, as you leave, shake off the dust that is on your feet as a testimony against them.”

verses.rationale: Retains repentance as the purpose of their proclamation.
verses.before: They went out and proclaimed that people should repent.
verses.after: They went out and proclaimed that people should repent.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they went out and proclaimed that people should repent.

verses.rationale: Keeps exorcism, anointing, and healing as distinct actions with repeated many.
verses.before: They cast out many demons and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.
verses.after: They drove out many demons and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and healed them.

verses.rationale: Follows plural people were saying and preserves the reported causal explanation rather than attributing it immediately to Herod.
verses.before: King Herod heard about Jesus, because his name had become well known. Some were saying, “John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work in him.”
verses.after: King Herod heard about Jesus, whose name had become well known. People were saying, “John the Baptist has been raised from the dead. That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: King Herod heard of it, for his name had become known. Some were saying, “John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, and for this reason these powers are at work in him.”

verses.rationale: Retains the three-way identity discussion and does not replace the last comparison with a certainty about a specific prophet.
verses.before: Others said, “He is Elijah.” Still others said, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of old.”
verses.after: Others said, “He is Elijah.” Still others said, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But others said, “It is Elijah.” And others said, “It is a prophet, like one of the prophets of old.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Herod’s emphatic personal responsibility and the resurrection claim as his speech.
verses.before: But when Herod heard, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has been raised.”
verses.after: But when Herod heard this, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has been raised!”
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Herod heard of it, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has been raised.”

verses.rationale: Signals the explanatory flashback and makes the marriage relationships explicit without adding external genealogy.
verses.before: Herod himself had sent men to arrest John and bind him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, whom Herod had married.
verses.after: For Herod himself had sent men to arrest John and bind him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, whom Herod had married.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Herod himself had sent and seized John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her.

verses.rationale: Preserves John’s repeated objection and its stated legal character without adding a legal citation.
verses.before: John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
verses.after: John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For John had been saying to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”

verses.rationale: Makes the grudge’s target clear and retains both lethal intent and inability.
verses.before: So Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to kill him, but she could not,
verses.after: Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Herodias had a grudge against him and wanted to kill him. But she could not,

verses.rationale: Follows pinned puzzled, not did many things, and preserves Herod’s conflicted response and protection.
verses.before: because Herod feared John, knowing he was a righteous and holy man, and protected him. When Herod listened to him, he was greatly perplexed, yet he still liked to listen.
verses.after: For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe. When he listened to John, he was deeply puzzled, yet he liked hearing him.
verses.tsw_comparator: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he protected him. And when he heard him, he was greatly perplexed; and yet he heard him gladly.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ominous opportunity and all three invited groups.
verses.before: An opportunity came on Herod’s birthday, when he gave a banquet for his officials, military commanders, and the leading people of Galilee.
verses.after: Then an opportunity came. On his birthday, Herod gave a banquet for his high officials, military commanders, and the leading men of Galilee.
verses.tsw_comparator: But an opportunity came when Herod on his birthday gave a banquet for his courtiers and officers and for the leaders of Galilee.

verses.rationale: Follows autēs tēs Hērōdiados as Herodias’s own daughter and does not import the alternative daughter-name reading.
verses.before: Herodias’s own daughter came in and danced, and she pleased Herod and his guests. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
verses.after: Herodias’s own daughter came in and danced, pleasing Herod and his dinner guests. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And when his daughter Herodias came in and danced, she pleased Herod and his guests; and the king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the oath and extravagant half-kingdom promise without treating it as a narrator’s legal claim.
verses.before: He swore to her, “Whatever you ask me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”
verses.after: He swore to her, “Whatever you ask me for, I will give you—even half my kingdom.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he swore to her, “Whatever you ask me, I will give you, even half of my kingdom.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the consultation and identifies both female speakers clearly.
verses.before: She went out and asked her mother, “What should I ask for?” Her mother said, “The head of John the Baptist.”
verses.after: She went out and asked her mother, “What should I ask for?” Her mother said, “The head of John the Baptist.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” She replied, “The head of John the Baptist.”

verses.rationale: Retains both urgency markers, the demanded platter, and immediate timing.
verses.before: The girl hurried back at once to the king and said, “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter right now.”
verses.after: At once she hurried back to the king and made her request: “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter, right now.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately she rushed back to the king and asked, saying, “I want you to give me at once the head of John the Baptist on a platter.”

verses.rationale: Keeps grief distinct from refusal to act rightly and retains both stated pressures.
verses.before: The king became deeply grieved, but because of his oaths and his dinner guests, he did not want to refuse her.
verses.after: The king was deeply grieved. But because of his oaths and his dinner guests, he did not want to refuse her.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the king was deeply grieved; yet because of his oaths and his guests, he did not want to refuse her.

verses.rationale: Names John and the executing guard for clarity and preserves the violence without euphemism.
verses.before: Immediately the king sent an executioner with orders to bring John’s head. The man went and beheaded John in the prison,
verses.after: At once the king sent a guard with orders to bring John’s head. The guard went and beheaded him in prison.
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately the king sent a soldier of the guard and ordered him to bring John’s head. He went and beheaded him in the prison,

verses.rationale: Retains the complete chain of transfer and repeated girl, avoiding a sanitized summary.
verses.before: brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the girl. The girl gave it to her mother.
verses.after: He brought the head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
verses.tsw_comparator: and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl. And the girl gave it to her mother.

verses.rationale: Names whose disciples act and preserves retrieval and burial.
verses.before: When John’s disciples heard, they came, took his body, and laid it in a tomb.
verses.after: When John’s disciples heard, they came, took his body, and laid it in a tomb.
verses.tsw_comparator: When his disciples heard of it, they came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.

verses.rationale: Retains apostles where it actually occurs in this pinned source, unlike the absent clause in 3:14.
verses.before: The apostles gathered around Jesus and reported everything they had done and taught.
verses.after: The apostles gathered around Jesus and told him everything they had done and taught.
verses.tsw_comparator: The apostles gathered around Jesus and told him all that they had done and taught.

verses.rationale: Keeps the private invitation, limited rest, and explanatory crowd pressure.
verses.before: He said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest for a while.” So many people were coming and going that they did not even have time to eat.
verses.after: He said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.” So many people were coming and going that they had no chance even to eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.” For many were coming and going, and they had no leisure even to eat.

verses.rationale: Repeats the destination and privacy while preserving travel by boat.
verses.before: They went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
verses.after: So they went away by themselves in the boat to a deserted place.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned recognition and arrival sequence without adding a later gathering clause.
verses.before: But many people saw them leaving and recognized them. They ran there on foot from all the towns and arrived ahead of them.
verses.after: But many saw them leaving and recognized them. People ran there on foot from all the towns and arrived ahead of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now many saw them going and recognized them, and they ran there on foot from all the towns and arrived ahead of them.

verses.rationale: Retains the stated ground of compassion and teaching as the immediate response.
verses.before: When Jesus came ashore and saw a large crowd, he had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So he began teaching them many things.
verses.after: When Jesus stepped ashore, he saw a large crowd and felt compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. He began teaching them many things.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when he went ashore, he saw a great crowd; and he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And he began to teach them many things.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated lateness in narration and speech rather than treating it as redundant.
verses.before: When it was already late, his disciples came to him and said, “This is a deserted place, and it is already very late.
verses.after: By then it was late. His disciples came to him and said, “This is a deserted place, and it is already late.
verses.tsw_comparator: When it grew late, his disciples came to him and said, “This is a deserted place, and the hour is now very late.

verses.rationale: Keeps both rural destinations and the disciples’ proposed purchase by the people themselves.
verses.before: Send the people away so they can go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
verses.after: Send them away so they can go to the surrounding farms and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Send them away, so that they may go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy something for themselves to eat.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic you and the exact monetary amount rather than an unstable modern equivalent.
verses.before: Jesus answered, “You give them something to eat.” They said, “Are we supposed to go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them?”
verses.after: But he answered, “You give them something to eat.” They said to him, “Are we to go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” And they said to him, “Are we to go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give it to them to eat?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the command to investigate and the separate food counts.
verses.before: He asked, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” When they found out, they said, “Five—and two fish.”
verses.after: He asked them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” When they found out, they said, “Five, and two fish.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” When they found out, they said, “Five, and two fish.”

verses.rationale: Makes the addressees explicit and retains the green grass and meal grouping.
verses.before: He told them to have everyone sit down in groups on the green grass.
verses.after: He told the disciples to have everyone sit down in groups on the green grass.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he ordered them to have all the people sit down in groups on the green grass.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two group sizes without imposing a total count from them.
verses.before: They sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties.
verses.after: They sat down in groups of a hundred and of fifty.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they sat down in groups of hundreds and of fifties.

verses.rationale: Preserves blessing rather than substituting thanksgiving and keeps the repeated giving and both food types.
verses.before: Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke the loaves, and kept giving them to the disciples to set before the people. He also divided the two fish among everyone.
verses.after: Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, and spoke a blessing. He broke the loaves and kept giving them to the disciples to set before the people. He also divided the two fish among them all.
verses.tsw_comparator: Taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven and blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before the people; and he divided the two fish among them all.

verses.rationale: Keeps the universal participation and satisfaction without adding a mechanism.
verses.before: They all ate and were satisfied.
verses.after: They all ate and had enough.
verses.tsw_comparator: And all ate and were filled.

verses.rationale: Retains twelve baskets and the fish remnants without counting an extra set of baskets.
verses.before: The disciples picked up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and fish.
verses.after: They gathered twelve basketfuls of broken pieces, as well as what was left of the fish.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and of the fish.

verses.rationale: Retains the specifically male count rather than silently substituting people.
verses.before: Those who ate the loaves numbered five thousand men.
verses.after: The men who ate the bread numbered five thousand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who had eaten the loaves were five thousand men.

verses.rationale: Keeps the force of made, the named direction, and the division of actions.
verses.before: Immediately Jesus made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him toward Bethsaida on the other side while he dismissed the crowd.

verses.before: Having eyes, do you not see? Having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember?
verses.after: You have eyes—do you not see? You have ears—do you not hear? And do you not remember?
verses.tsw_comparator: Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember?

verses.rationale: Preserves the first feeding’s linked numbers and ordinary basket term.
verses.before: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of pieces did you pick up?” They said, “Twelve.”
verses.after: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of pieces did you gather?” They said to him, “Twelve.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They said to him, “Twelve.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the second feeding’s different linked numbers and larger basket term in the recollection.
verses.before: “And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many baskets full of pieces did you pick up?” They said, “Seven.”
verses.after: “And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many large baskets full of pieces did you gather?” They said, “Seven.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “And the seven for the four thousand, how many baskets of broken pieces did you take up?” And they said, “Seven.”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated not-yet question and leaves it unanswered.
verses.before: He said to them, “Do you still not understand?”
verses.after: He said to them, “Do you still not understand?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Do you not yet understand?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the arrival, the man’s condition, and others’ request on his behalf.
verses.before: They came to Bethsaida. People brought a blind man to Jesus and begged him to touch him.
verses.after: They came to Bethsaida. People brought a blind man to Jesus and begged him to touch him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the private movement, exact bodily actions, and diagnostic question without euphemism.
verses.before: Jesus took the blind man by the hand and led him outside the village. After spitting on his eyes and laying his hands on him, he asked, “Do you see anything?”
verses.after: Jesus took the blind man by the hand and led him outside the village. He spat on the man’s eyes, laid his hands on him, and asked, “Can you see anything?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Taking the blind man by the hand, he led him outside the village. After spitting on his eyes and laying his hands on him, he asked him, “Do you see anything?”

verses.rationale: Preserves partial sight and the unusual walking-tree comparison rather than summarizing blurred vision.
verses.before: The man looked up and said, “I see people; they look like trees walking around.”
verses.after: The man looked up and said, “I can see people. They look like trees walking around.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Looking up, he said, “I see people, because I see them like trees walking around.”

verses.rationale: Preserves again and the threefold account of restored sight rather than erasing the two stages.
verses.before: Then Jesus placed his hands on the man’s eyes again. The man looked intently, his sight was restored, and he saw everything clearly.
verses.after: Then Jesus laid his hands on the man’s eyes again. The man saw clearly; his sight was restored, and he could see everything distinctly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he again laid his hands upon his eyes, and he looked intently, and his sight was restored, and he saw everything clearly.

verses.rationale: Follows the short pinned prohibition without adding an instruction about telling others.
verses.before: Jesus sent him home and said, “Do not even go into the village.”
verses.after: Jesus sent him home, saying, “Do not even go into the village.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent him to his house, saying, “Do not even enter the village.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the named district, plural villages, and question asked during the journey.
verses.before: Jesus and his disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “Who do people say that I am?”
verses.after: Jesus and his disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “Who do people say I am?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus went out with his disciples to the villages of Caesarea Philippi, and on the way he was asking his disciples, saying to them, “Who do people say that I am?”

verses.rationale: Preserves all three reported identifications without adding adjectives to prophets.
verses.before: They told him, “John the Baptist; others say Elijah; still others, one of the prophets.”
verses.after: They answered, “John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and others, one of the prophets.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they told him, saying, “John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and others, one of the prophets.”

verses.rationale: Makes the emphatic you audible and retains the confession without importing Matthew’s added title.
verses.before: He asked them, “But you—who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”
verses.after: He asked them, “But you—who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Messiah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he asked them, “But you—who do you say that I am?” Peter answered and said to him, “You are the Christ.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the force of rebuke and the command’s scope without explaining the secrecy.
verses.before: Jesus strictly ordered them not to tell anyone about him.
verses.after: He sternly warned them not to tell anyone about him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he strictly ordered them that they should tell no one about him.

verses.rationale: Preserves must, all three rejecting groups, death, and after three days without harmonizing on the third day.
verses.before: Then he began teaching them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and after three days rise.
verses.after: Then he began teaching them that the Son of Man must suffer greatly, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and rise after three days.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes and be killed, and after three days rise.

verses.rationale: Keeps open speech and Peter’s private rebuke in explicit contrast.
verses.before: He spoke this word openly. Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
verses.after: He spoke about this openly. Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he was speaking the word plainly. Then Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.

verses.rationale: Retains the disciples as witnesses, reciprocal rebuke, Satan address, and contrast of orientations.
verses.before: But Jesus turned, looked at his disciples, rebuked Peter, and said, “Get behind me, Satan! You are not setting your mind on the things of God but on human things.”
verses.after: But Jesus turned, saw his disciples, and rebuked Peter. “Get behind me, Satan!” he said. “You are not thinking about God’s concerns, but human concerns.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But turning and seeing his disciples, he rebuked Peter and said, “Get behind me, Satan, for you are not setting your mind on the things of God but on the things of human beings.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the widened audience, conditional invitation, and all three demanding actions without softening the cross.
verses.before: Jesus called the crowd together with his disciples and said, “If anyone wants to come after me, let that person deny themselves, take up their cross, and follow me.
verses.after: He called the crowd to him along with his disciples and said, “If anyone wants to come after me, they must deny themselves, take up their cross, and follow me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Calling the crowd with his disciples, he said to them, “If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the save–lose reversal and both named grounds for loss.
verses.before: For whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for my sake and for the good news will save it.
verses.after: For whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me and for the good news will save it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the good news will save it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the commercial contrast and life consistently with the preceding verse.
verses.before: What does it profit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit their life?
verses.after: What does it profit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit their life?
verses.tsw_comparator: For what does it profit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?

verses.rationale: Retains the unanswered exchange question and the recurring life term.
verses.before: What can a person give in exchange for their life?
verses.after: What could a person give in exchange for their life?
verses.tsw_comparator: For what can a person give in exchange for his life?

verses.rationale: Preserves reciprocal shame, the generation’s severe description, and all elements of the coming scene without interpretive expansion.
verses.before: Whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of that person when he comes in his Father’s glory with the holy angels.”
verses.after: For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of them when he comes in his Father’s glory with the holy angels.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy messengers.”
